misses.why: Berk et al 2024, employer-based short-term savings. Closest published setting to a liquid round-up pot; effect sizes here transfer better than pension estimates do.
Thaler & Benartzi 2004, Save More Tomorrow. The escalation design that made the preset-level question a design decision rather than a parameter.
Jachimowicz et al 2019 meta-analysis of default effects, with moderators. The pooled effect size the brief asked for instead of a single study's estimate.

Carroll, Choi, Laibson, Madrian & Metrick 2009 (QJE). The paper that put required active choice on the table as an alternative to a default rather than a weaker version of one — which is precisely the third option the brief is deciding between.
